conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I’m Dr. Lee. I’ll be your doctor during this stay. You’re here for abdominal pain and vomiting that came back after eating tacos last night?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, exactly. I was feeling great after my last hospital visit—no pain, no meds. But last night, it all came back suddenly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. And you mentioned going to the ED, but they sent you home. Then your mom found you passed out in your vomit?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes. I felt awful. I didn’t pass out on purpose—I just collapsed. I was so dizzy and nauseous.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That sounds scary. We’ll make sure you’re stable. Your vitals are okay now—blood pressure a bit low at 100/60, heart rate 95, but not alarming.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve had POTS for years—my heart rate jumps when I stand. Is that related?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, POTS can cause that. We’ll keep an eye on it. You’re on betaxolol, right? That helps control your heart rate.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I take it every day. But the abdominal pain is what worries me the most.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Understood. You have a history of chronic pancreatitis. You had part of your pancreas removed a few years ago, which helped for a while.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, the surgery helped a lot. But lately, the pain keeps coming back, even without drinking or eating fatty foods.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve reviewed your CT scan from today. It shows no acute issues—no inflammation, blockages, or new problems in the abdomen.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: But the pain is real. Why can’t they see anything?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I believe you. Sometimes chronic pain doesn’t show up on scans. We’ve seen this before with chronic pancreatitis—even without active inflammation, nerves can stay sensitive.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So it’s just in my head?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No, not at all. The pain is real. But because tests are normal, some doctors have wondered if anxiety or stress might be making it worse. That doesn’t mean it’s not physical.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I do have anxiety, yes. But I don’t think that’s causing the vomiting or passing out.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re right. Passing out like that needs attention. We think it could be from dehydration or a POTS flare, especially with nausea and poor intake.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That makes sense. I hadn’t eaten much before the tacos.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve started IV fluids to help with that. We’re also giving you IV Dilaudid for pain and Zofran for nausea.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: The pain is already better. Thank you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. We’ll keep you NPO—nothing by mouth—for now, to let your gut rest. We’ll reassess tomorrow about eating.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. How are you feeling today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Better. Nausea is gone, and I haven’t needed pain meds since last night.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. We’re going to try a clear liquid diet—water, broth, apple juice. If you tolerate that, we can move to soft foods.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Can I have tea? I usually drink it with lemon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, weak tea without milk is fine. Start small—just a few sips. Let the nurse know if you feel any nausea.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve done well with liquids. We’re upgrading you to a soft diet—applesauce, toast, yogurt. How’s your energy?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Still tired, but I’m not dizzy when I sit up. My face feels warm though—could that be a fever?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You do have a mild facial rash and low-grade temperature. Given your Sjogren’s, this could be a mild flare. We’ll monitor it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve had this before. It usually goes away with rest. Should I call my rheumatologist?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we recommend you follow up with your PCP or rheumatologist this week. We’ll continue your Plaquenil and prednisone.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What about the H. pylori treatment? I started it once but stopped because I was vomiting.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Right. You never really completed the course. We’re keeping you on omeprazole for now. Call your PCP to restart the antibiotics when you’re ready.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’ll do that. I just don’t want another flare like this.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good news—you’ve been tolerating food well, no pain or nausea. We’d like to discharge you today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Really? That’s great. But what if the pain comes back?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: If pain or vomiting returns, call your doctor or come back. We’re sending you home with acetaminophen for pain or fever.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my other meds? Should I restart everything?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, resume all your home medications—Plaquenil, prednisone, betaxolol, amitriptyline, and the pancreatic enzymes. We’ve updated your list.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I’ll follow up with my doctors and take it slow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and don’t hesitate to reach out if anything changes.
